newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hokkaido Takushoku says lent Y47.4 bln to Tokai.
newsitem.headline: Hokkaido Takushoku says lent Y47.4 bln to Tokai.

text.p: Japan's Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd said on Friday that Tokai Kogyo Co Ltd had outstanding loans to the bank totalling 47.4 billion yen and that they may not be recoverable.
Tokai Kogyo earlier filed a request for court protection from creditors under Japanese bankruptcy laws.
Hokkaido Takushoku said in a statement that the loan figure, which also includes unpaid interest, accounted for 0.4 percent of its total assets as of March 1997.
The bank also said that it plans to write off its estimated loss of some 30 billion yen arising from its loans to Tokai in the April-September period.

The said said the planned write-off was unlikely to have any major impact on the bank's earnings in the financial year to March 1998, because the loss would be offset by profits from a planned sale of shareholdings.

Hokkaido Takushoku announced last month that it would discuss cooperation in several areas with Britain's Barclay's Bank, including the development of new financial products and securitisation of the Japanese bank's assets.
